labels.why: Salesforce governor limits (callout timeout, callouts, heap, CPU) bind any implementation that calls an external model.
Async callouts run on platform job queues with hard enqueue/concurrency limits, so some requests can fail to enqueue.
The model's context window is finite, so a long conversation must be trimmed or summarised at some size.
Input length is bounded by the model context and Salesforce field/payload sizes, so a maximum must exist.
Beyond the platform timeout, a latency target is a product choice; the bot answers correctly without one.
An unbounded waitlist works correctly; capping it is a product decision.
Promotion cannot sensibly happen after the class starts, so some cut-off (at latest the start time) must be defined.
Promotion is correct as long as it happens before the cut-off; a tighter latency bound is a product choice.
Automatic reminders need a defined count and timing; without it they never send or repeat endlessly.
Any email/SMS provider enforces a send rate, so large batches must be paced within it.
Reminders sent at any hour still work; restricting sending hours is a product preference.
Reminders function without a volume cap or lateness bound; imposing one is a product decision.
Uploads and in-memory parsing are bounded by request size and server resources, so a maximum must be stated.
The request does not say whether creating users sends mail at all; if it does, provider limits would apply.
The import is correct however long it takes; a duration bound and progress display are product choices.
